instructions: Pat the shrimp dry. Peel and devein them if they aren't already.
Wipe the guajillo chiles with a damp paper towel. Cut off the stems, shake out the seeds and slice the chiles into thin strips. Slice the garlic thinly. Juice the limes.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, stirring often, until it's pale gold. Don't let it brown.
Add the chile strips and stir for 1 minute, until they smell toasty.
Add the shrimp in a single layer and sprinkle them with the salt. Pour in the wine and lime juice.
Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until the shrimp are pink and curled into a loose C. Take the pan off the heat.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Serve straight from the pan.
method_notes: No version of this dish had 20 or more ratings, so the lead is the most complete one I could read (In Mama Maggie's Kitchen, 5 from 1 vote); no trusted-cook version exists. Sources agree on garlic and sliced guajillo cooked briefly in fat before the shrimp go in, and lime to finish. Maggie's uses butter; olive oil replaces it to keep the dish dairy-free, as Slender Kitchen's and Lucy Waverman's versions use olive oil too. The árbol chile is left out to keep it mild; add it at the table if wanted.
